title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires that any artificial‑intelligence system used in Virginia be clearly labeled and its decision‑making process explained to users. It sets up rules for developers and companies to provide accessible information about how their AI works and how it may affect people, aiming to keep AI tools honest and understandable for everyone.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act aims to ensure that artificial intelligence used in Veterans Affairs claims processing is transparent, fair, and reliable. It establishes oversight, accountability, and recourse mechanisms so that veterans can trust the AI tools that evaluate their benefits.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act is a proposed law that aims to protect the integrity of elections by preventing the use of AI-generated content to mislead voters. It would set rules and penalties for creating or sharing AI‑driven misinformation that could influence election outcomes.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a federal law designed to set clear, rigorous standards for AI systems so they are reliable, safe, and transparent. It requires developers to conduct thorough testing, follow oversight rules, and report potential risks to protect users and maintain public trust.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to shield shoppers from misleading claims made by AI-driven products and services. It requires businesses to clearly disclose when content is AI-generated, keep representations accurate, and give consumers a way to seek redress if they’re deceived.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act establishes guidelines and requirements for the development and deployment of artificial intelligence systems to ensure they meet stringent security and risk mitigation standards. It aims to protect users, data, and infrastructure by mandating rigorous testing, transparency, and accountability for AI developers and operators.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act creates a dedicated task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to oversee and strengthen the security of artificial intelligence systems. The act defines the task force’s duties—such as developing security guidelines, coordinating with industry and government stakeholders, and ensuring AI technologies meet stringent safety and resilience standards.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 establishes comprehensive guidelines to identify, assess, and mitigate risks associated with AI systems, ensuring that developers implement robust security measures and adhere to best practices. It also creates an oversight body to enforce compliance, promote transparency, and protect the public from potential harms stemming from AI technology.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act aims to regulate and coordinate the deployment of physical systems powered by artificial intelligence, ensuring safety and interoperability across industries. It establishes guidelines, certification requirements, and oversight mechanisms to promote responsible development and deployment of AI-driven robots and machines.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard the integrity of elections by regulating the use of artificial intelligence in political messaging. It seeks to prevent AI-generated misinformation and ensure voters are not misled by deceptive content during campaign periods.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act is a law designed to keep track of artificial intelligence systems that can change and learn on their own. It requires developers and users to report how these AI systems evolve, ensuring they remain safe, reliable, and in line with regulatory standards.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act aims to curb the risks posed by uncontrolled or harmful artificial intelligence. It proposes strict oversight, safety standards, and possibly bans for AI systems that could cause significant harm.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act would temporarily halt the construction and operation of large AI data centers to address concerns about their environmental impact, energy use, and regulatory oversight. The law would set a pause period during which experts could assess risks and develop guidelines before any new AI data center projects could resume.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The act creates a Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to oversee and probe cyber incidents involving artificial intelligence systems, ensuring thorough and coordinated responses. It sets guidelines for data protection, incident reporting, and collaboration between federal agencies to strengthen national security and promote responsible AI use.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is designed to promote the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence technologies that benefit the U.S. population. It seeks to encourage innovation, protect privacy and security, and ensure AI tools are aligned with American values and economic growth.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act is a new law that requires companies and organizations in China to regularly submit detailed reports on their AI systems, covering capabilities, usage, and the amount of energy they consume. This measure is intended to promote transparency, ensure compliance with national standards, and help the government monitor the development and impact of artificial intelligence across the country.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a law that restricts the use of artificial intelligence in medical practice. It requires that all medical decisions be made by qualified human doctors, preventing AI systems from replacing or supplanting human medical professionals.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The proposal creates a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the President’s Executive Office to monitor, assess, and mitigate risks from AI and other cutting‑edge technologies. It also aims to coordinate policy, research, and collaboration across government agencies to protect national security and public interests.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution creates a new Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence that will be tasked with studying and guiding the nation's AI initiatives. The committee will evaluate AI developments, address policy and ethical concerns, and recommend actions to promote responsible and beneficial use of artificial intelligence.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: This act requires companies that create or deploy AI systems to assess and disclose the potential risks of their technology. It establishes a regulatory framework for monitoring, auditing, and enforcing compliance, with penalties for non‑compliance.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 establishes a comprehensive framework for the development, deployment, and oversight of artificial intelligence systems, aiming to promote safety, transparency, and accountability in AI technologies. It sets specific regulations for high‑risk AI applications, defines standards for data quality and algorithmic fairness, and creates enforcement mechanisms to ensure compliance with national and international norms.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a law that requires businesses that create and use AI to measure and reduce the environmental harm they cause. It establishes guidelines for tracking carbon emissions, energy usage, and waste, and it gives regulators the power to enforce these rules.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: This act aims to ensure that K‑12 students have the skills and knowledge to understand and responsibly use AI technologies. It outlines programs, curriculum standards, and resources to support AI literacy and readiness in schools.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 aims to establish rigorous standards and oversight for AI research, ensuring that systems are safe, trustworthy, and aligned with societal values. It introduces requirements for transparency, risk assessment, and collaboration between researchers, regulators, and stakeholders to promote responsible AI development.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to launch a pilot program that employs artificial intelligence to defend critical infrastructure from cyber attacks. It also includes broader provisions aimed at strengthening the security and resilience of the nation’s essential systems.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a federal law that requires schools to integrate AI education into their curriculum, ensuring students learn about AI concepts, ethics, and applications from an early age. It also provides funding and training for teachers, updates technology infrastructure, and promotes equitable access so all students can develop digital literacy skills needed for the future workforce.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act is a legislative proposal aimed at increasing public understanding and knowledge of artificial intelligence. The act seeks to establish educational initiatives, outreach programs, and resources to help people grasp AI’s benefits, risks, and impact on society.
